purpose: W5-A: extend the existing settlement PostgreSQL authority with one canonical FinancialObligation view and explicit multi-scheme SettlementPlan router while retiring competing mutation semantics instead of creating a second ledger.
authorization: Owner instruction on 2026-09-05 to continue the supplied PC-CROP post-registration specification with existing push/PR/merge authorization. Implementation remains blocked until this finite scope is independently accepted and promoted into immutable base-state authority.

excludedAfterSourceAudit.reason: The first W5-A foundation builds obligation/plan authority beside existing settlement facts without changing production command routing; consumer wiring is a later accepted slice.
Mounted HTTP behavior remains unchanged in the foundation.
Federal Accounting lock #4321 and accounting authority are read-only source evidence for W5-A; this programme does not mutate that locked scope.
Authoritative money remains in the private settlement schema. No new public Prisma ledger model is introduced.
Global CI remains an independent gate.
Generic additive migration checker remains unchanged.

requiredInvariants: Extend the existing settlement schema/payment_terms/beneficiaries/payments/holds/bank_operations/hash-chain ledger authority; do not create LedgerV2 or another money source of truth.

FinancialObligation is a canonical immutable/versioned statement of who owes whom, amount/currency, basis, payer, payee, due conditions, source revisions and lifecycle state. It is not inferred from UI labels or environment defaults.

Obligations may represent commodity consideration, logistics/service charges, platform fees, taxes/withholding or adjustments only when backed by accepted Commercial Rules, Deal/service facts and explicit payer authority.
Service provider selection or payer assignment alone does not create an obligation; payer confirmation and the applicable rule/contract basis are distinct required evidence.

SettlementPlan is versioned and routes exact obligations through one or more settlement schemes, including direct bank payment, safe-deal/escrow-like reserve-release, offset/netting, advance/prepayment, post-payment or manual external settlement reference when policy allows.

Every plan pins scheme policy version, obligations, beneficiaries, exact amounts, release/hold conditions and provider-independent capability requirements. A bank/provider name is never core settlement semantics.
Plan totals and obligation allocations conserve exact minor units. No Float money, hidden fees, unversioned defaults or browser totals become authority.
A plan revision creates a new immutable version. Confirmed bank operations/hash-chain ledger entries and historical obligations are never rewritten.

Current tenant, Deal participant, organization, membership, payer and required authority are revalidated before mutation and replay; revoked authority cannot replay an old obligation/plan receipt as current authorization.
Same-tenant outsiders and cross-tenant actors cannot read private obligation/plan details outside explicit Deal/accounting/bank authority.
Every accepted obligation/plan mutation commits version, immutable event, audit and outbox atomically with payload-bound idempotency and optimistic concurrency.
Legacy/global-memory ledger mutation paths must not receive new authority; later consumer migration must route all new monetary truth through settlement before retirement.
Registration, Role Eligibility, Federal Accounting lock #4321, Commercial Rules, Service Marketplace, W2/W3 work, packages/lockfiles and production topology remain unchanged.
acceptance: Restricted PostgreSQL tests prove creation/versioning of multiple obligation types and a SettlementPlan whose exact allocations sum to the exact obligation set.
Payer assignment without explicit confirmation/rule basis cannot create a payable obligation; conflicting payer/rule evidence fails closed.
Multi-scheme plans preserve provider-neutral semantics and can map the same obligation model to at least two policy schemes without core schema changes.
Changed source facts/rules produce a new obligation/plan version while preserving the previous immutable version and ledger/bank history.
Cross-tenant/same-tenant outsider access, revoked payer/member authority, stale version and changed-payload replay are denied.
Audit/outbox/event failure rolls back all obligation/plan rows and receipts.
No public Float-money or process-memory ledger path is introduced or used as authority in W5-A tests.
Forward migrations, zero public-schema drift, restore, cryptographic freshness, global CI and exact-head review pass while accounting lock #4321 remains untouched.
remainingTerminalBoundary: Mounted Settlement API and migration of every current payment/service/Deal consumer to the canonical obligation/plan authority remain later work.
Actual multi-bank/Sber adapters and provider receipts remain EXT-01 and do not receive terminal credit here.
Accounting document generation/reconciliation must consume the obligation view without duplicating money authority.
Verified REG.RU runtime and real financial-flow acceptance remain required before FINANCIAL_LEDGER/SETTLEMENT_PLAN terminal PASS.
